title: RENAAL — Losartan in Type 2 Diabetic Nephropathy
subtitle: N Engl J Med · 2001
summary: Blocking the renin-angiotensin system with losartan slowed the decline toward kidney failure in people with type 2 diabetes and nephropathy, independent of its blood-pressure effect. It helped establish angiotensin blockade as a cornerstone of diabetic kidney protection.

title: IDNT — Irbesartan in Diabetic Nephropathy
subtitle: N Engl J Med · 2001
summary: Irbesartan protected the kidneys of hypertensive type 2 diabetics better than either amlodipine or placebo, and the benefit went beyond blood-pressure lowering. Together with RENAAL it made angiotensin-receptor blockers standard therapy in diabetic kidney disease.

title: SPRINT — Intensive vs Standard Blood-Pressure Control
subtitle: N Engl J Med · 2015
summary: Targeting a systolic pressure under 120 rather than under 140 cut cardiovascular events and deaths, though at the cost of more acute kidney injury and electrolyte problems. It reshaped how aggressively clinicians treat blood pressure, including in many patients with CKD.

title: CREDENCE — Canagliflozin in Diabetic Kidney Disease
subtitle: N Engl J Med · 2019
summary: The first trial designed around kidney endpoints showed an SGLT2 inhibitor markedly reduced kidney failure and cardiovascular events in type 2 diabetics with established nephropathy. It launched SGLT2 inhibitors as disease-modifying kidney drugs rather than just glucose-lowering agents.

title: DAPA-CKD — Dapagliflozin in Chronic Kidney Disease
subtitle: N Engl J Med · 2020
summary: Dapagliflozin slowed kidney disease and reduced deaths in people with CKD whether or not they had diabetes, extending SGLT2 benefit well beyond diabetic nephropathy. The result pushed these drugs into the core of CKD care generally.

title: EMPA-KIDNEY — Empagliflozin in Chronic Kidney Disease
subtitle: N Engl J Med · 2023
summary: In the broadest CKD population studied for an SGLT2 inhibitor, empagliflozin reduced progression and cardiovascular death across a wide range of kidney function and causes. It solidified SGLT2 inhibition as a near-universal option for slowing chronic kidney disease.

title: FIDELIO-DKD — Finerenone in Diabetic Kidney Disease
subtitle: N Engl J Med · 2020
summary: The non-steroidal mineralocorticoid-receptor antagonist finerenone lowered kidney and cardiovascular events in type 2 diabetics already on maximal angiotensin blockade, with less hyperkalemia risk than older agents. It opened a distinct therapeutic pathway on top of existing standard care.

title: TEMPO 3:4 — Tolvaptan in Polycystic Kidney Disease
subtitle: N Engl J Med · 2012
summary: Tolvaptan slowed the relentless growth of kidney cysts and the loss of function in autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease, the first therapy shown to alter its course. Its benefit has to be weighed against thirst, frequent urination, and liver-enzyme monitoring.

title: MENTOR — Rituximab vs Cyclosporine in Membranous Nephropathy
subtitle: N Engl J Med · 2019
summary: Rituximab was better than cyclosporine at achieving and, crucially, maintaining remission of proteinuria in membranous nephropathy over two years. The durability of response moved B-cell depletion toward first-line treatment for this glomerular disease.
